_why_this_package_exists: Haage & Partner's Euro-Update for AmigaOS 2.1+ - updated keymaps, updated
bitmap fonts and updated `.country` files, so that Alt-E types the Euro
sign. It is row 7 of the AmigaOS 3.9 chain and the one row the material
itself declares redundant under row 8: BoingBags 3&4's own readme lists
*"These official updates are incorporated: Euro-Update, ShellUpdate 45.39"*.
So it is worth having only where BoingBags 3&4 will not be installed - see
_why_the_tree_measured: Read with 7-Zip 26.02 on 2026-09-08 from the owner's own
Euro-Update/C/FixFonts, C/Installer         its own bundled helpers
And `Euro-Update/Euro-Install` itself, read in full, does exactly four
things after asking for a volume:
The nine `.country` files the brief asked about are there and are placed:
belgie, belgique, deutschland, españa, france, italia, nederland, portugal,
österreich. **`Workbench/Locale/Flags/Keymaps` is shipped and never copied**
by the package's own script; ART does not place it either, because doing
more than the artefact's own installer does is ART inventing a step nobody
name: Euro-Update for AmigaOS 2.1+
_why_no_distinguished_by: `Euro-Update` is this archive's own single top-level directory and no other
archive in the owner's folder claims it (the same 44-archive pass
distinguisher that separates nothing can only refuse an archive that would
have worked - `boingbag-39-1`'s own recipe states the rule.
_why_chain_position_and_requires: 7 of the material's own order. `requires` is **empty**, and that is the
measurement rather than an oversight: the archive's own `Readme` says
*"Euro-Update for AmigaOS 2.1+"* and *"to support the Euro currency on
AmigaOS version 2.1 or higher"*, and `Euro-Install` checks no version at
all - it asks for a volume and copies. So no BoingBag has to be on the
tree first. It is placed at 7 because that is where the chain shows it,
not because anything before it is required.
_why_superseded_by: BoingBags 3&4's own readme, read from the owner's `BoingBags3&4.lha` on
ShellUpdate 45.39"*. So a tree that has had BoingBags 3&4 installed
already carries this, and the chain row reads *not needed* rather than
*missing* - which is the difference between telling somebody to go and
find a file and telling them they already have what is in it.
The direction is deliberate: the **older** package names the newer one, so
a package added later never has to be edited to keep this true.
_why_host_placement_block_needs_fixfonts: **The decision this recipe exists to record, and it went the other way.**
The brief asked whether ART can rebuild the `.font` index files the
package's own installer rebuilds with `FixFonts`, and to declare a block
only if it cannot. It cannot, and here is what was read.
`grep -rn '\.font' src-tauri/src/core` (2026-09-08) finds `.font` in three
places - `apply.rs` and `recipe.rs`, which check that a *placed* descriptor
is spelled `.font` exactly because `diskfont.library` matches the suffix
case-sensitively (ART-225), and a test fixture in `source.rs`. Nothing in
ART parses or writes a `FontContentsHeader`. The layered-release and
locale rounds placed descriptors as opaque bytes; neither built one.
**What building one would take, measured rather than recalled.** The ten
descriptors in this archive were dumped byte by byte and compared with the
tree ART's own AmigaOS 3.9 build produced. Each is `0f 00`, an entry count,
then 260-byte entries of a 256-byte name, a `ysize`, a `style` and `flags`:
`courier.font` is 1304 bytes for 5 sizes on both sides, `ruby.font` 784 for
3, `helvetica.font` 1564 for 6. Every family names exactly the sizes that
tree already has, and nine of the ten differ from the tree's **only in
entry order** (this archive lists `courier/24` first, the tree lists
`courier/11` first); `topaz.font` is byte-identical. The `flags` byte is
not constant - `0x42` for courier, `0x62` for ruby - and it comes from each
size file's own `DiskFontHeader`, a second binary format ART has never read
and has no independent oracle for.
**So why block at all, if the rebuild is a no-op on that tree?** Because
that is a measurement about *one* tree. On a tree whose `Fonts` drawer
holds a size this archive's descriptor does not name, placing the
descriptor removes that size from the index: the size file stays on disk,
nothing fails, nothing is logged, and a font quietly stops being available.
ART cannot ask an arbitrary tree that question, and a half-placement that
boots is this project's most expensive defect. The row is therefore
untickable and says why, which is what section 89 asks for - never hidden,
and never silently short.
The rules below are still declared, and they are what a future
`rebuild-font-index` step would place the day somebody measures a
`FontContentsHeader` writer against real material.
_why_no_amiga_installer: `Euro-Update/Euro-Install` is an Installer **script**, not a program, and
`AmigaInstaller::program` is a path to a program inside the package. The
script asks `askdir` for the target volume and `confirm`s every copy, so
nobody knows whether it finishes without a person at the window either.
Declaring `program: "C/Installer"` would be worse than declaring nothing:
the archive's `C/Installer` is the helper the *script* is run by, and
naming it here would tell the engine to launch an installer with no script
_why_overrides: Every destination below is one the AmigaOS 3.9 recipe already writes:
`WORKBENCH3.9/DEVS` and `LOCALE`, `keymaps` the CD's own keymaps and
`locale-euro` the CD's `LOCALE.EURO/COUNTRIES`. This package replaces files
at those paths on purpose - that is what an update is - so the components
are named rather than left for a later stage to read as a surprise, the
same call `boingbag-39-1`'s own recipe records at length.
